h1: The 8 Best Nightstands with Charging Station of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Nightstands with Charging: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: eight nightstands with built-in charging for 2026, compared on outlets, USB-C ports, size, drawers and lighting.
summary: The Huuger rustic nightstand is the best overall, with two AC outlets, USB-A, USB-C and two fabric drawers in a 15.7 inch width. The VASAGLE CUSTOS has five ports and a 99 lb top. The SUPERJARE adds an adjustable drawer, and the LED models from Huuger, Lazzanto and Fixwal add lighting. The ADORNEVE hides its charging station and the JARHETUN is a matching pair.
intro: Most shoppers count outlets and ignore the footprint, then find the nightstand will not fit the gap beside the bed. Width and depth are the first checks, because a 23.6 inch nightstand is a different piece of furniture from a 15.7 inch one, and a charging model that crowds the bed gets unplugged and moved within a month. Ports come second, since USB-C is what a current phone uses to charge quickly.

Our editors reviewed eight nightstands with built-in charging and ranked them on dimensions, port mix, storage, lighting and safety hardware. Scores follow the listings. Where a maker says USB without naming USB-C, we count the port as unconfirmed, and models that cannot show a clear port list lose ground.

products.name: Huuger Nightstand with Charging Station, Rustic Brown
products.verdict: A straightforward charging nightstand with 2 AC outlets, USB-A and USB-C.
products.description:
This Huuger measures 15.7 inches wide, 11.8 deep and 23.6 high, and offers two AC outlets, one USB-A jack and one USB-C jack. Two fabric drawers and an open shelf handle storage, and the P2 particleboard and powder-coated steel frame has adjustable feet. USB-C matters because most current phones charge fastest over it.

It wins because it covers the essentials without extras that can fail, in the $25 to $50 bucket. Against the SUPERJARE it adds a second drawer, and against the LED Huuger it skips the lighting.

Buy it for a no-fuss charging nightstand. The caveats: the tabletop is small, and there is no lighting. If you want a lamp plus a phone plus a book on top, a wider surface like the VASAGLE's will suit you better.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a charging nightstand without extras.

products.name: VASAGLE CUSTOS Nightstand, Ink Black, 23.6" Wide
products.verdict: 5 ports in total, a 99 lb top load rating and the widest surface here.
products.description:
The CUSTOS is 23.6 inches wide, 13.8 deep and 24.1 high, with five charging ports in total: two wall outlets, two USB-A jacks and a USB-C jack. A 99 lb tabletop load rating means a lamp, a clock and a stack of books will not trouble it, and the finish is water and scratch resistant. App-controlled LED lighting and gold handles complete it.

It ranks second because it is the largest and costs more, in the $50 to $100 bucket. The width is the problem in a narrow bedroom.

Buy it for the widest surface and the most ports in one piece. Skip it if the gap beside your bed is narrow. At 23.6 inches it needs a deliberate amount of floor.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want the most charging ports and the widest surface in one nightstand.

products.name: SUPERJARE Nightstand with Adjustable Drawer, Rustic Brown
products.verdict: A fabric drawer with 2 positions and 3-tier open shelves.
products.description:
The SUPERJARE is 15.7 inches wide, 11.8 deep and 23.4 high, with one USB-A, one USB-C and two AC outlets. Its fabric drawer has two positions, so it adapts to items of different heights, and three open shelves sit below. A stain resistant finish keeps spills from marking the top.

It ranks third because the drawer adapts to different items, which the Huuger's fixed drawers do not, but it has only one drawer. The ports match the Huuger exactly, at the same $25 to $50 price.

Buy it if you want a drawer that adjusts and open shelves for books. Skip it if you want two drawers. The caveat: the small top limits what stands on it, and it has no lighting, so a bedside lamp will take most of the surface.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a drawer that adapts to different item sizes.

products.name: Huuger Night Stand with LED and Charging Station, Black
products.verdict: The Huuger design with 60,000 colors, music sync and 12 scenes.
products.description:
This Huuger shares the 15.7 by 11.8 by 23.6 inch frame and the same two outlets plus USB-A and USB-C as the rustic model, and adds LED lighting with 60,000 colours, music sync, app control and 12 scenes. Two fabric drawers hold small items.

It ranks fourth since the lighting is an extra over the first model, not a replacement for it. If you like a glow at night, the LED earns its place. If you do not, you are paying for a feature you will switch off.

Buy it for ambient lighting you can control from your phone. Skip it if you prefer a plain look. The caveat is that lighting adds an app and a wiring harness to manage, and the small tabletop remains. It sits in the same $25 to $50 bucket.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want app-controlled ambient lighting built in.

products.name: Lazzanto Nightstand with LED Strip, Black
products.verdict: LED strip with app, timer, voice control and music sync.
products.description:
The Lazzanto is 15.6 inches wide, 11.4 deep and 24.4 high, with two USB ports and two AC outlets. An LED strip works with an app, a timer, voice control and music sync, and the top is water-resistant with rounded corners. Two fabric drawers handle storage.

It ranks fifth because the USB ports are listed without a USB-C count, unlike the Huuger. Voice control and the timer are the distinguishing features, which suit people who like to dim the room without reaching for a phone.

Buy it if you want voice-controlled LED lighting and a timer. Skip it if you need a confirmed USB-C port. The caveat: without USB-C stated, a newer phone may charge slowly over USB-A. Ask the seller to confirm the port type before ordering, at $25 to $50.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want voice-controlled LED lighting with a timer.
products.skipIf: You need a confirmed USB-C port.

products.name: Fixwal Night Stand with RGB LED, Black
products.verdict: A narrow, deep footprint of 11.8 by 15.7 inches with a 5 ft cord.
products.description:
The Fixwal is 11.8 inches wide and 15.7 deep, 23.6 high, with two AC outlets and two USB ports. An RGB LED with a music sync app adds lighting, two fabric drawers and a two-layer shelf store things, and a 5 ft cord reaches a distant wall socket.

It ranks sixth because its USB count lacks a confirmed USB-C, but the narrow width fits tighter bedside gaps than the 15.7 inch wide models. The unusual orientation, deeper than it is wide, means it suits a narrow gap with floor to spare.

Buy it for a tight space beside the bed. Skip it if you have no depth to spare, since it projects 15.7 inches into the room. The 5 ft cord is useful, but check that it reaches your socket.
products.idealFor: Tight bedside gaps where a narrow, deep footprint fits.
products.skipIf: You have no depth to spare.

products.name: ADORNEVE White Nightstand with Sliding Top Charging Station
products.verdict: A sliding top hides the charging station until you need it.
products.description:
The ADORNEVE is 17.72 inches wide, 15.75 deep and 23.62 high, in engineered wood. A sliding top reveals a hidden charging station with two outlets and two USB ports, and it adds an RGB LED app and two drawers. When closed, the top is a clean surface with no visible cords.

It ranks seventh because it costs more, in the $50 to $100 bucket, than the basic Huuger for a similar port count. The hidden station is the reason to pay extra, for a bedroom that wants a tidy look.

Buy it if you hate visible plugs. Skip it if you want the cheapest option. The caveat: USB-C is not confirmed, and a sliding mechanism is one more moving part. Before ordering, confirm the cord length and where the cable exits.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a charging station hidden until needed.

products.name: JARHETUN Night Stand Set of 2 with LED, Black
products.verdict: Two matching nightstands, each with its own ports and LED.
products.description:
The JARHETUN set contains two tables, each 15 inches wide, 11.2 deep and 26.4 high, with two USB and two AC outlets per table. Each has an RGB LED with app and music sync, three fabric drawers, a metal mesh fence and an anti-tip kit. The pair costs $50 to $100.

It ranks last only because few buyers need two. For those who do, a matched pair with ports on each side is hard to beat, and the per-table price is competitive.

Buy it for a couple who want charging on both sides of the bed. Skip it if you only need one nightstand. The caveats are that USB-C is not confirmed, and the 26.4 inch height is taller than the others, so check it against your mattress. Install the anti-tip kit.
cons: Need two for it to pay off
products.idealFor: Buyers who need matching charging nightstands on both sides of the bed.

whatMatters.detail: AC outlets run lamps and chargers, USB-A suits older cables and USB-C suits newer phones and tablets. A nightstand without USB-C limits fast charging on current devices. Check the port list in the specifications, and note which listings only say USB. Count how many devices you charge overnight, and add a spare, since a partner's phone needs a port too.

The listings range from 11.8 to 23.6 inches wide. A piece that does not fit the gap is a return. Measure the gap beside the bed before buying, including how far the drawer opens and where the bed leg sits. Note that depth varies too, and the Fixwal is deeper than it is wide, so check both dimensions.

Fabric drawers hold small items, and open shelves keep books in reach. Decide what you keep beside the bed, then choose between drawers, shelves or both. Check the drawer and shelf counts in the listing. Fabric drawers are lighter than wooden ones and tend to sag if overloaded, so keep heavy items on the shelf.

LED strips add ambience, but they also add an app and wiring to manage. Plain models are simpler and have fewer parts that fail. Check whether the listing mentions LED, voice control or app control, and whether you want those features. If you share a bedroom, a light that switches on by voice can irritate a sleeping partner.

A lightweight nightstand can tip, which matters with children. An anti-tip kit anchors it to the wall. Look for it in the listing, since only the JARHETUN states one here. If a kit is not included, buy a strap, because a tipped nightstand can pull its cords out of the wall.

faq.q: Do all charging nightstands have USB-C?
faq.a: No. The Huuger, SUPERJARE and VASAGLE list USB-C, while several others list only USB. Confirm the port type before ordering, because a newer phone charges faster over USB-C than USB-A.

Skipping the measurements. The listings range from 11.8 to 23.6 inches wide, and the gap beside most beds is smaller than people think. Measure the width, depth and height first, and compare them with the Huuger's 15.7 inch width.

faq.q: Is the VASAGLE worth it over the Huuger?
faq.a: If you want five ports and a 99 lb top, yes. The Huuger is smaller and costs less, and covers the basics with two outlets, USB-A and USB-C. The VASAGLE earns its price only if you use the extra ports.

faq.q: How do I set up the lights?
faq.a: LED models use an app. Follow each listing's pairing steps, and keep the app on your phone. Lighting models such as the Huuger LED, Fixwal and JARHETUN also list music sync, so test the settings before bedtime.

faq.q: Do I need an anti-tip kit?
faq.a: It is wise with children or pets. The JARHETUN set includes one. For other models, buy a wall strap and anchor the nightstand to the wall. Check the strap tension every few months.

faq.q: Can I clean the top easily?
faq.a: The Lazzanto lists a water-resistant top and the VASAGLE lists water and scratch resistance. Wipe the others with a dry cloth and avoid leaving damp cups on the top, and keep liquids away from the outlets.

finalTake: Buy the Huuger rustic for a simple charging nightstand, or the VASAGLE if you want the most ports and the widest top. Choose the Fixwal for a narrow gap, the ADORNEVE for a clean top, and the JARHETUN when both sides of the bed need power. Measure the gap before you order.
